messages.subject: Hierarchical structure for traffic-related exposures
parts:
Dear all,

I'd like to carry out a conditional logistic regression using case-control data. I am trying to assess the impacts of pollution on a particular health outcome:

logit(y) = a + b1 * traffic1 + b2 * traffic2 + b3 * traffic3 + c * PM + d * Ozone + Covariates 

I'd like the effects (b1, b2, b3) of the traffic-related exposures (traffic1, traffic2, traffic3) to be random effects with a hierarchy, with the random effects from a shared distribution with N(0, sigma^2).

Currently I am running this via the below, but the values for b1,b2,b3 will not have any hierarchy. Because they are from the same source (traffic), I would like to, as said above, add a hierarchy:

Could anyone please advise on how I would include the hierarchy in this situation? I would be extremely grateful!

formula = ck ~ f(stratum,model="iid",hyper=list(theta=list(initial=log(1e-6),fixed=T))) +
         traffic1 + traffic2 + traffic3 + PM + Ozone +
         covariates +

# function to run INLA model
inla_run = function(formula, data){
  mod = inla(formula, family='Poisson', 
           control.family=list(link='log'),
           control.predictor=list(link=1, compute=TRUE),
           control.compute=list(dic=TRUE),
           data = data)
  
  return(mod)
  
}

model_output = inla_run(formula, data)

Thank you!

Robbie

messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Hierarchical structure for traffic-related exposures
parts:
If you want it like you wrote it, you need

idx.na = rep(NA, n)
traffic1 = 1:n
traffic2 = n + 1:n
traffic3 = 2*n + 1:n

... f(idx.na, model="iid",values=1:(3*n)) +
f(traffic1, b1, copy="idx.na") +
f(traffic2, b2, copy="idx.na") +
f(traffic3, b3, copy="idx.na") + ...


the first 'f()' defines the random effects, with length 3*n, but since
idx.na are all NA, its not in use.

the other ones, uses the correct part of the random effect with weights
b2, say (I guess b2 is a vector),

please check it out first on a simulated example

H

parts:
It would probably be easier to set this up with inla.stack than with "copy.
Something like this:

stack <- inla.stack(data=list(ck=ck), A= list(cbind(traffic1, traffic2, traffic2),1), effects = list(list(b = 1:3),list(stratum=stratum, PM=PM, Ozone=Ozone))
formula = ck ~ f(stratum, ...) + f(b, model="iid", n=3) + PM + Ozone
inla(..., control.predictor=list(A=inla.stack.A(stack)), data = inla.stack.data(stack))

Finn
